doc.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: How she writes music
summary: She composes on the flute and checks the changes at a keyboard.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. And hope the conductor knows where you are too. Do you write music at a keyboard?

I don’t own a piano so generally speaking I write it with my flute, I run the changes, and then I sit at a keyboard at some point when I’m starting to get it put together and play the changes to make sure that’s what I want.
So you play the changes on your flute, up and down, and you can hear if that’s in the ballpark of what you want.

In the ballpark, and then it takes me actually doing it at the piano to make sure that I’m right and I sometimes don’t have quite the right voicing or the right changes, but I at least have an idea of what gender of chord I want there. I’ve been looking at keyboards and things, I just hate the sound of them, the little portable keyboards. I probably need to get one of those.
